analysis:
The only changed file is docs/architecture/inference.md. Per file_changes, the changes are a date bump, a rewrite of GLM5Next video handling (variable-frame-rate video is now indexed at i / nominalFrameRate instead of refused with a deterministic 400), and a small addition around lines 876-880 that is outside the supplied units. The two units are the unchanged tail of the document (lines 1215-2035): prefill geometry, deadlines, MTP, sampling, reasoning parsers, tool parsing, vision caps, and the MiMo candidate. I found no changed lines in them, and nothing in them alters a security control.

The threat model relevant here is T-041 (prefix cache), A-001 (prompts) and TB-007. Line 1901 still says vision requests never stage SSD blocks. The changed GLM text says media requests are excluded from prefix lookup and capture, which is consistent with the T-041 cache-isolation posture. Nothing here touches the HMAC lookup tags, TTL, account-scoped cacheSalt or KEK purge. The narrative lines 1713-1715 say the sampler is not part of cache identity, which is unchanged.

The doc change describes a behavioral change in the GLM5Next processor: VFR video is accepted rather than refused. I could not verify that code in the supplied evidence, so I record it as an unverified contract. Possible concerns are the media decoded-byte caps (maxMediaDecodedBytes, the 512 MiB maximumDecodedBytes) and DoS bounds on VFR indexing. The doc states the frame cap and the 28,532 visual-token cap still apply. A later pass should confirm that the implementation matches these bounds. The docs change itself introduces no regression, so I report no findings.
